A.explanation: This is half the weight and ignores that only $F \sin 30^{\circ}$ provides the upward moment about X.

B.explanation: This uses $F \cos 30^{\circ}$ for the vertical component instead of $F \sin 30^{\circ}$ for a $30^{\circ}$ angle to the horizontal.

C.explanation: Taking moments about X gives $F \sin 30^{\circ} = 5.0 \text{ N}$, so $F = 10 \text{ N}$.

D.explanation: This doubles the correct value, from incorrectly balancing $F \sin 30^{\circ}$ against the full $10.0 \text{ N}$ at the centre rather than at half the rod length.

hints: Notice the rod is uniform, so its $10.0 \text{ N}$ weight acts vertically down at its midpoint, a distance $L/2$ from hinge X.
Only the component of $F$ perpendicular to the horizontal rod can balance the clockwise moment of the weight about X.
Take moments about X so the hinge force has no moment, then equate the anticlockwise moment $F \sin 30^{\circ} \times L$ to the clockwise moment $10.0 \text{ N} \times L/2$.
walkthrough: Take moments about hinge X because the unknown hinge force then has zero moment and is eliminated.
The weight $10.0 \text{ N}$ acts at the centre of the uniform rod, so its clockwise moment is $10.0 \times L/2$, where $L$ is length XY.
Force $F$ acts at Y at $30^{\circ}$ to the horizontal rod, so its perpendicular distance effect is from the vertical component $F \sin 30^{\circ}$.
Its anticlockwise moment about X is therefore $F \sin 30^{\circ} \times L$.
For equilibrium, sum of moments about X is zero: $F \sin 30^{\circ} \times L = 10.0 \times L/2$.
Cancel $L$ and use $\sin 30^{\circ} = 0.5$: $0.5F = 5.0$, so $F = 10 \text{ N}$. This is option C.
